key_insight: The PAGE framework uses AI to parse, annotate, and explain comics at archive scale, enabling new quantitative studies of visual storytelling across American comics and Japanese manga.
engineering_relevance: This paper shows how multimodal document AI can transform large, scanned cultural archives into searchable, analyzable datasets while preserving links to human-coded validation.
method: Parse every page into panels, text, and bibliographic metadata
Use a vision-language model guided by a written codebook for page annotations
Ground model outputs with human annotation and estimate change while controlling for publisher and genre
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on 3,929 American comic books (1938–1956) and 87 Japanese manga volumes across three studies, with results checked against human annotation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of scans and codebook consistency, and archive-level comparisons must account for publisher and genre confounding.
paper_title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
